Class 1 · Chapter 7 of 8

Coins, prices and change

Count coins and notes and work out what you need.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Read clocks and calendars. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can add coin values.
  • I can total two prices.
  • I can work out my change.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Every coin has a value

Our coins are worth Rs 1, Rs 2, Rs 5 and Rs 10.

Big number on the coin, big value.

Screen 2 of 4

Add them up

A Rs 10 coin and a Rs 5 coin.

10 and 5 make 15. Altogether it is Rs 15.

Screen 3 of 4

Notes are worth more

Notes are worth Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 50 here.

A Rs 20 note and a Rs 5 coin make Rs 25.

Screen 4 of 4

Change

A pencil costs Rs 7. You pay with Rs 10.

Change is what comes back: 10 − 7 = 3. You get Rs 3.

Words to know
coin
A small round piece of money.
note
A paper piece of money.
change
The money you get back when you pay more than the price.

Chapter passed. Next: Sort, order and solve picture clues

For parents

What your child learns

Coins have different values. To pay an exact price, add coin values until you reach it. Each item has a price, so find how many you can buy by sharing the money into equal prices.

A common slip

Children often count the coins, not their values. Write the value under each coin and add the values. Then check the total matches the price.

5-minute home activity: Pay exactly

  1. Use real or paper coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10.
  2. Pay Rs 8 using exactly 3 coins.
  3. Pay Rs 17 using exactly 3 coins.
  4. Share Rs 12 into items that cost Rs 2 each and count how many.
